chunks: From him, from his father or someone else, from Harun ibn Harija, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about supplication and raising the hands, so he said: 'It is upon four aspects. As for seeking refuge (al-ta'awwudh), face the Qiblah with the inner side of your palms. And as for supplication regarding sustenance, extend your palms and direct their inner sides towards the sky. And as for devotion (al-tabattul), it is a gesture with your index finger. And as for invocation (al-ibtihal), it is raising your hands so they exceed your head. And the supplication of humility (al-tadarru') is that you move your index finger from what faces your face, and it is the supplication of the fearful one.'
ai.seo_question: What are the different ways to raise hands during supplication in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates four distinct postures for supplication, linking specific hand gestures to their spiritual intent: facing the Qibla with palms inward for seeking refuge, raising open palms for sustenance, pointing the index finger for devotion (tabattul), and raising hands above the head for intense beseeching (ibtilal). This classification highlights the Shia emphasis on the physical manifestation of inner states, where the orientation of the hands reflects the degree of humility and urgency in the believer's communication with the Divine.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father or someone else, from Haroun Bin Kharija, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the supplication and raising of the hands, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is upon four aspects – As for the seeking of Refuge, so face the Qiblah with the front of your palms; and as for the supplication regarding the sustenance, so extend your palms and display their backs towards the sky; and as for the devotion, so gesture with your index finger; and as for the invocation, so raise your hands to exceed your head by them; and the beseeching supplication is that you move your index finger from what follows your face, and it is a supplication of the fearful one’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father and others from Harun ibn Kharijah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about prayer and raising hands. The Imam said, ‘It is in four ways: in al-Ta’awwuz (seeking refuge) turn the palms of your hands toward the Ka’bah and in prayer for sustenance stretch your hands with their palms upward to the sky. Al- Tabattul is gesturing with index finger. Al-Tbtihal is to raise both hands over your head with prayer and imploration. Moving your index finger before your face is in prayer when one is fearful.’”
